description: Which CI jobs a changed file needs. select-test-scope.ps1 matches every changed file against these rules in order; the first rule whose pattern matches decides. A rule lists the jobs the file needs, or "all". A file no rule matches, a change other than an addition or modification, an empty diff and a diff that cannot be computed all run every job. Patterns are relative to the repository root, case-sensitive, with forward slashes: * matches within one folder, ** across folders, and **/ at the start also matches the root. The focused rules rely on dependencies that scripts/ci/ci-job-plan.test.js checks against the repository; see docs/operations/testing.md (Job selection).

rules.why: Workflows, CI and release scripts (this planner included), the solution, project, MSBuild and NuGet files and Git attributes change how every job builds or checks.
Wasla.UnitTests reads these documents (WaslaConfigurationKeyTests) or checks their working-tree state (WaslaVisualFoundationTests).
No .NET project compiles these files and no .NET test reads them. The terminology guard and the Node tests run for every change.
Only Wasla.UnitTests compiles or reads the files of its own folder.
Only Wasla.PrintBridge.Tests compiles or reads the files of its own folder.
Only the Print Bridge job builds the installers, and only Wasla.PrintBridge.Tests reads their sources. The MSBuild files of the folder match ci-and-build first.

Wasla.UnitTests compiles Wasla.Web; Wasla.PrintBridge.Tests reads Web views, scripts and resources, and Wasla.PrintBridge embeds the Web logo.
Both test projects compile Domain, Application and Infrastructure: persistence and migrations, tenant isolation, authentication services and provider clients.
Wasla.PrintBridge.Tests compiles the Print Bridge projects; Wasla.UnitTests reads their resources and sources and scans every file under src/.
